lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

measurements.units: CSS px at 96 dpi from geometry.json (1 px = 0.265 mm)

margins.note: Three sides are equal. The right margin is intentionally taken by the monument. The channel between the text and the monument (33.8 px, 8.9 mm) is narrower than the gutter (36 px), so the monument crowds the right column's prices instead of framing them.

headers.result: pass on size and x. Sub-head level fails consistency: Beer's 'DRAFT' is set inline on the head line, while every other sub head sits on its own row, so one level has two treatments.

item_pitch.note: 65.2 px = 2.64u and 46.2 px = 1.87u. Neither is a whole multiple of u, so the claimed baseline grid is not a true grid.

price_pair_scan_pct_of_column.result: fail_remote_prices, which caps criterion 3 at 40. The Old Fashioned name ends 14.3 px (3.8 mm) from its price, a near-collision in the same column where other rows travel 43 mm.

contrast_worst_pixel.note: The ground is flat with no art behind any text, so the worst pixel equals the ground.

dead_space.note: There is a 37 mm dead field under Amber Lager with no job. The right column is holed where Brut Rose, the tequilas and Cognac have no description lines.

bleed.result: pass on the geometry, but no bleed file was produced

visual_tests.note: The accent sits below the 0.4-6% range of the references and reads as timid.

top_problem: The design is ref-02 panel 4 with its art removed: a default Oswald 700 word set sideways, with no image system, material or cultural idea. It fails the substitution test: any cantina, and any bar, could use the same page unchanged. The boldest missing idea is a monument that carries the venue itself, for example Mexican wood-type or rótulo-derived letterforms cut by hand, or a chile-red overprint or impression that carries the materiality of the reference boards. Instead it is a Google Fonts headline.
remove: The 'GOOD DRINKS / GOOD PEOPLE' tagline stack. It is lifted verbatim from the reference boards as costume, says nothing about this venue, and only fills the dead lower-left corner instead of solving it.
fixes: Cut eye travel: narrow the left column's price measure to about 45 mm or set prices a fixed 4 mm after the name. Either removes the 10 rows over 40% and the 3.8 mm Old Fashioned near-collision.

Give the monument an art direction: bespoke or wood-type-derived letterforms and a print materiality (letterpress bite, riso chile-red overprint, or a real image in the counters) tied to a thesis that names Mexico and Iowa City. The wordmark must stop being swappable Oswald 700.

Join the name into one phrase: move '& COCKTAIL BAR / IOWA CITY, IOWA' to the monument's foot or start, rotated or aligned to its baseline. The ampersand currently begins a sentence whose first word sits 130 mm away across the page.

Rebalance the columns: widen the channel to at least 2x the gutter by shaving the right column or reducing the crop. Then end both columns within one u of each other so the 37 mm dead field under Amber Lager is closed.

Make each hierarchy level consistent: treat Beer 'DRAFT' like every other sub head, or remove single-item sub heads (Sparkling, Brandy, Draft) everywhere. Snap item pitch to whole multiples of u so the baseline grid is real.

lens: items/prices vs draft rev 3, ingredient names and description completeness (public_components honoured), section flow for an Iowa City Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar
top_problem: Descriptions are uneven and incomplete. The four cocktails get full ingredient lines, but four items (Brut Rosé, Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila, Cognac VSOP) have no description at all. Beers have no ABV, and wines have no region (Brut Rosé has no grape either). The draft descriptions were cut down to one-word stubs ('Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Sparkling'). None of the unknown facts is flagged `missing_ingredients`: the proposal only raises a soft 'trimmed_descriptions' question. The 14 items and 14 prices match the draft exactly, and Aromatic Bitters is correctly hidden on the Manhattan. But half the menu tells the guest nothing the item name has not already said. Iowa City wordmark aside, that is a price list, not a menu.
problems: Criterion 8: Brut Rosé, Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP print no description. Dropping an 'echo' is noted, but nothing was added in its place and no missing facts were requested (spirits need a brand or producer and age statement; the rosé needs grape and region).

Criterion 8: beers have no style/ABV line ('Toasty', 'Hop-forward' are fragments with no ABV) and wines have no region. These unknowns are not flagged `missing_ingredients` as scorecard criterion 8 requires.

Criterion 10: the menu uses two naming conventions: 'Tequila blanco' in the Margarita line vs 'Blanco Tequila' as the item name. It also says 'demerara syrup' (Daiquiri) but 'demerara' (Old Fashioned). Description depth runs from four-ingredient lines to one word to nothing, so the content voice does not hold together.

Criterion 5: in the letter layout, the first text the eye reads after the monument is '& COCKTAIL BAR'. It opens with an ampersand whose noun (CANTINA) sits rotated across the page, so the entry reads as a fragment. There are also dead bands: about 190 css px between the sub-line and Cocktails, and a large gap under Amber Lager. Cider stands alone as a one-item section after Spirits instead of next to Beer. Beer's 'DRAFT' rides on the head line while every other sub head gets its own row, so one hierarchy level has two treatments.
Criterion 5: item pitch is uneven. Rows without descriptions (Spirits, Brut Rosé) sit tighter than described rows, so the right column's rhythm stutters.

Criterion 3: prices are consistent (whole numbers, no $, tabular, right-aligned per column), but eye travel is long. In the left column, Manhattan, Margarita, Czech Pilsner and Amber Lager run about 55-60% of the column span with no leader or row rule (in the right column, Malbec runs about 54%). This goes past the ~40% price-pair flag. The gate still passes only because the rows are well isolated vertically and the absolute hop is about 40 mm, but this is at the edge of fix_remote_prices.

Content integrity check: all 14 names and prices match the draft (15, 15, 14, 16, 7, 8, 7, 12, 11, 13, 12, 16, 18, 8). Nothing is invented. The Manhattan leaves out bitters as public_components requires. The Old Fashioned (house_recipe=false) shows names only. 'Good drinks / Good people' and '& cocktail bar / Iowa City, Iowa' state no item facts.
fixes: Give every item a description line, and flag every unknown as `missing_ingredients` (beer ABV; wine region, plus grape for the Brut Rosé; brand/producer and age for Blanco, Añejo and Cognac VSOP) instead of silently printing nothing or one-word stubs.

Until those facts arrive, restore the draft's complete, sourced descriptors instead of fragments: 'Crisp pale lager', 'Hop-forward IPA', 'Toasty amber lager', 'Dry red', 'Dry white', 'Dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry sparkling cider'. Style words are what the scorecard asks for, even when they partly echo the name.
Make the terms consistent: use 'Blanco tequila' (or 'Tequila blanco') in both places, and 'demerara syrup' in both cocktail lines.

Fix the reading path: set the sub-line as 'CANTINA & COCKTAIL BAR' (or drop the ampersand) so the entry is not a fragment. Move Cider directly under Beer in the left column (or merge it as 'Beer & Cider' with the Coordinator's approval). Give 'DRAFT' its own sub-head row to match every other sub head.

Shorten price eye travel in the left column: narrow the name-to-price measure (about 200 css px), or add a hairline row rule so no row goes past 40% of the span without a guide. Also equalise item pitch so rows without descriptions keep the same baseline step.

lens: Every printed ingredient and label traced to build/draft_doc.json (revision 3) and phg.menu_items/phg.recipe_versions (gateway log_id 210); how descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png and geometry.json
top_problem: Every price sits in the far-right column with no leader or row rule, and the direction's own avoid-list bans leaders. In the left column the gap between name and price takes up 55-62% of the 262 px measure: Margarita name ends x=135.5 and its price starts x=296.8 (62%), Manhattan 58%, Amber Lager 57%, Czech Pilsner 55%. Malbec in the right column is 53% of 170 px. On the phone it gets worse: Malbec 86.5 to 306.8 is 73% of 300 px. Meanwhile Brown Butter Old Fashioned ends at x=282.5 and its 16 starts at 296.8, only 14 px later, so that price reads as part of the name. Under scorecard 4 this fails menu_item_association. Behind this is a venue problem. Apart from the wordmark, this is a generic American bar list. The Margarita comes second, under a Manhattan. Agave spirits sit below wine in the right column. No heading uses Spanish, and nothing on the page says Mexican restaurant.
problems: Checked and sourced (content_integrity pass): Manhattan 'Rye whiskey · sweet vermouth · cocktail cherry' = draft_doc beta_manhattan components Rye Whiskey/Sweet Vermouth/Cocktail Cherry. Aromatic Bitters is correctly hidden by meta.public_components.aromatic-bitters=false. Cocktail cherry also matches phg.recipe_versions 9fb77eaa… garnish 'Cocktail cherry'.

Checked and sourced: Margarita 'Tequila blanco · lime · orange liqueur · agave' = draft desc and components of beta_margarita (recipe_version f06abb74…). House Daiquiri 'White rum · lime · demerara syrup' = components of beta_daiquiri (14d45e57…); dropping 'house' is allowed. Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Brown butter-washed bourbon · demerara · bitters' = draft desc of beta_old_fashioned word for word; house_recipe=false is respected.

Checked and sourced: every price matches phg.menu_items.menu_price (15/15/14/16/7/8/7/12/11/13/12/16/18/8). Accents 'Añejo' and 'Rosé' match the source spelling. 'Good drinks / Good people' is generic and states no item fact.

The '& COCKTAIL BAR / IOWA CITY, IOWA' line and the CANTINA wordmark do not trace to draft_doc: title is 'Bar menu' and no venue name is given. The only source is the direction brief. It is venue copy, not an item fact, so it is not a gate fail, but it needs a named input. The kicker also starts with '&' at the top left, so it reads before the word it joins, which is the vertical wordmark at the far right.

Criterion 11 detail: nothing the draft or recipe_versions supplies beyond ingredients is printed. Glass and garnish from phg.recipe_versions go unused: Margarita Rocks / Lime wheel, Daiquiri Coupe / Lime coin, Old Fashioned Rocks / Orange peel on a large cube. No beer style/ABV, wine region or spirit age/pour size exists in the source, and the proposal does not flag missing_ingredients for them. The result is accurate but thin.

Descriptions (criterion 12): 'Toasty', 'Hop-forward', 'Dry red', 'Dry white' and 'Sparkling' are cut-down leftovers. 'Hop-forward' is an adjective with no noun. 'Dry red' and 'Dry white' are category labels, not guest language. Brut Rosé, Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP have no description at all. That leaves three voices: middot ingredient lists, one-word fragments and silence.

Venue fit (criterion 13): the Margarita sits under the Manhattan in Classics. Agave is a small subhead in the right column below Wine, and there are only two tequilas. The only lager is a Czech one. Headings are all English (no Cócteles, Cervezas, Agave y más). Item 'Blanco Tequila' and description 'Tequila blanco' reverse the word order on the same page. The name 'CANTINA' is the only Mexican signal.

Pour labels (criterion 14): Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Sparkling', not 'By the Glass', and the draft price label is empty, so a guest cannot tell glass from bottle. The spirits prices have no pour size (the draft has none either, so flag it instead of guessing).

Data sync: phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b… has 15 rows, including 'Junmai Ginjo' 12 'Junmai Ginjo sake.'. draft_doc revision 3 and the design have 14. This is not an error in this design, but the Coordinator should confirm which item list is current.
fixes: Pull each price in beside its name with a fixed 1.5 em gap, or add a hairline row rule or dot leader under each name/description pair, so no row's eye travel exceeds 40% of the measure on letter or phone and the Old Fashioned's 16 stops touching its name.

Make the menu read Mexican from the draft's own items: put Margarita first in Classics and move Agave up so it leads Spirits, right after Cocktails and Beer. Add Spanish subheads from a named input, and keep 'Tequila Blanco' word order the same as the component row in draft_doc beta_margarita.

Replace the one-word fragments with the full draft descriptions ('Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Toasty amber lager.', 'Dry sparkling cider.') or a sourced guest-language line. Give Brut Rosé and the spirits a one-line description written only from their source facts, rather than printing nothing.

Add the sourced serve details from phg.recipe_versions to the cocktail lines, for example 'lime wheel' on the Margarita and 'orange peel · large cube' on the Old Fashioned. Flag missing_ingredients to the Coordinator for beer style/ABV, wine region and spirit pour size.

Label the Brut Rosé price (glass or bottle) and the spirits pour size once there is a source for them, and get the venue name/kicker ('Cantina', '& Cocktail Bar') confirmed as a named input, not only the direction brief.
